Where Every Child Thrives
At Yateley Manor, childhood is celebrated and potential is nurtured. From Nursery through to Senior School, every child is encouraged to grow in confidence, curiosity and character, supported by a school community that believes in their unique talents.
A journey through curiosity, confidence and care
Discover how Yateley Manor inspires children at every stage of their education. Explore our Nursery, Pre-Prep, Prep and Senior Schools to see how each step builds strong foundations for lifelong learning.
Pre-Prep
Why Choose Yateley Manor
A place where every child is known, valued and inspired
Yateley Manor combines academic ambition with genuine care. Our small class sizes, dedicated teachers and broad co-curricular offer ensure every child is supported to achieve their best and find joy in learning.
Excellence Backed by a Legacy of Learning
As a part of the Inspired Learning Group, Yateley Manor School draws from the collective strength of over 30 schools across the UK. This gives our students access to a wider network, richer resources, and innovative learning pathways.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts | Drama, Dance and Expression at Yateley Manor
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts at Yateley Manor
The Performing Arts are a vibrant and much-loved part of school life at Yateley Manor. From class assemblies and LAMDA examinations to whole-school productions, every pupil is encouraged to take part and express themselves.
Drama and Performance
Drama encourages imagination, empathy and teamwork. Many pupils choose to take LAMDA exams, which develop confidence and clarity in communication.
Each year, pupils take part in a range of performances – from imaginative class plays to full-scale productions in our drama studio. The Yateley Manor Youth Theatre and Youth Dance groups offer additional opportunities to perform and collaborate creatively.
Dance
Dance is taught from the earliest years, with Ballet available in Pre-Prep and a broad range of modern and contemporary classes as pupils move up the school. Through the performing arts, pupils learn not just how to perform, but how to present themselves with assurance, creativity and joy.

Facilities
How to Book Yateley Manor's Facilities
Our facilities, which include the sports hall, swimming pool and pitches as well as Drama Studio, Gym, Music School and Manor Place Hall, are available for hire, either by clubs and organisations or by individuals. Used regularly by local sports clubs and interest groups, we have also hosted events ranging from bridal fairs to national chess competitions. To view our full range of available facilities, please scroll down the page. To book any our our first class facilities we have on offer, please click the button below
Why should you book Yateley Manor's Facilities?
Children need space to learn and at Yateley Manor our extensive grounds provide the perfect facilities to inspire and challenge every child. The Creative Arts and Languages Centre provides state-of-the-art facilities in bright and spacious classrooms. The Music Technology Suite allows children to produce digital music with keyboards connected to computers and the six practice rooms provide ample space for individual and group rehearsals.
The indoor swimming pool is in use all year round. Behind Manor House and Manor Court, the main school building, the spacious sports hall, with its impressive cricket nets, football, netball and basketball facilities, is complemented by a second gymnasium and numerous sports pitches.Imaginatively equipped play areas give children the freedom to unwind and play creatively. There are a whole host of physical activities to try, including Dance and Ballet in our specially equipped Studio.
Opportunities to use the Berry Cooking Centre are timetabled regularly. Younger children learn how to cook basic meals and understand good food hygiene whilst older children cook across the curriculum in different subjects. This includes preparing food using rationing principles in History lessons and having a complete lesson taught in French, with oral instructions and recipes in the language.
Outdoor learning can boost children’s welfare and their performance at school. Spending time interacting with nature can boost children’s creativity and problem-solving skills. Our Woodland Learning Area has been designed to capitalise on these benefits and, together with the expertise of fully trained staff, the facility really brings out a different side of children.
A climbing wall and an Aeroball frame are popular recent additions to our facilities both donated by FYMS (Friends of Yateley Manor School).
What facilities do we have available to book?
Fyson Blum Hall
Our large modern sports hall is equipped with four full size indoor cricket net bays suitable for use with a hard ball.
The hall also has floor markings for
The Hall is also used for concerts and assemblies and has a seating capacity for 400 people and a large AV screen.
4 badminton courts
5-a-side football court with goals
short tennis
Swimming Pool
The swimming pool is a 16 metre indoor teaching pool which has a depth of 0.8m at one end and 1.5m at the other end and is ideally suited to teaching young children. It can be divided into three sections across the pool or four lanes and the school regularly hosts swimming galas. The pool is heated to a comfortable 86 degrees Fahrenheit (30 degrees Celsius) and is also used for kayak practice.
Gymnasium
The gymnasium has a resilient floor and is equipped with mini gymnastic equipment.
It is regularly hired out for activities such as martial arts, exercise classes and dance classes.
Studio
The studio is a small theatre/dance studio and is used for dance clubs and small productions. It has a raised area at one end and adjustable staging at the other. It also has a ballet barre on two walls and can seat 100 people.
Manor Place Hall
A multi-purpose hall with AV screen located in the Manor Place building. It is used for a variety of activities including music recitals and performances, presentations and workshops.
It is also ideal for hiring for dance or exercise classes, parties and martial arts. A small kitchenette and toilets are located just off the hall and tables and chairs are also available.
Music School and Tech Suite
The new Music School affords a large teaching room and six bright and airy practice rooms as well as a separate percussion room. A music technology suite allows pupils to use keyboards to record pieces into computers for manipulation through the software.
Berry (Cookery Room)
Being able to cook is a life skill and yet it is a skill which is becoming more and more marginalised in schools. At Yateley Manor we are passionate about preparing children for adult lives and cookery is one such skill. Basic cookery starts in our Nursery classes and children develop an awareness of hygiene and cookery utensils as they move through Pre Prep classes. In later years children use the facility to broaden and contextualise their learning across the curriculum, such as cooking in language and science lessons.
The Cuisine Centre can accommodate a class comfortably, with individual sinks and ovens. Our MasterChef clubs after school are very popular.
No matter how proficient a child is at cookery, they will enjoy the practical nature of cookery and enjoy the end results.
Fields and Pitches
Yateley Manor has a range of courts and outside grass areas which can be used for netball, tennis, hockey, rounders, cricket, rugby or football depending on the season. In the summer the fields are also set out for athletics including a five lane 300m grass running track and long jump pit.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School at Yateley Manor | Years 7-9
pageCache.text:
Senior School at Yateley Manor
It’s where pupils evolve — often transforming from quiet observers into confident young people who feel ready to take centre stage in their learning and school life. Our aim is to ensure every pupil flourishes across these years: academically, socially and personally.
Manor Place & Senior Hub
A dedicated Senior base with study areas, lockers and social spaces designed to support focus, friendship and self-reliance.
Specialist Classrooms & Labs
Fully equipped science, design and computing facilities allow pupils to experiment, innovate and explore ideas in depth
Sport & Fitness Facilities
Exceptional pitches, courts and a fitness suite provide the setting for teamwork, resilience and a lifelong love of sport.
Creative & Performing Arts Spaces
From music rooms and drama studios to art and DT workshops, our creative facilities encourage imagination and expression.
Years 7 & 8 – A Formative Stage
These early senior years are full of opportunity and development. Specialist teaching becomes the norm, enabling pupils to deepen skills across subjects with renewed focus and ambition. Pupils continue to hone foundational skills through the Prep School Baccalaureate core programme while exploring new horizons — enquiries, challenges and creative tasks become central to everyday learning.
Small tutor groups foster strong relationships with staff, enabling personal guidance and mutual respect. The focus is as much on character and confidence as it is on academic progress.
Beyond the Classroom
Trips & Expeditions
Where learning meets the real world. From Normandy to New Scientist Live, fieldwork and residential trips broaden horizons and deepen understanding far beyond the classroom.
Enrichment and Leadership
Where confidence and character take centre stage. Through mentoring, school committees and ambassador roles, seniors learn to lead, collaborate and make a lasting contribution.
Sport and Challenge
Where resilience and teamwork thrive. A dynamic sports programme, academies and competitions inspire every pupil to push boundaries, play fair and perform with pride.
Creative and Performing Arts
Where imagination becomes expression. From concerts and productions to art and design showcases, senior pupils develop creative confidence and the courage to perform.
Looking Ahead – The Path to GCSE
At Yateley Manor, we challenge pupils to aim high. For many, Years 7-9 lay the groundwork for their GCSE years (10-11). With our forward-thinking outlook, we already offer GCSE options in subjects such as PE to younger pupils, showcasing our commitment to stretching each individual.
Our growing Senior School is built around high academic standards, small class sizes and outstanding teaching — all underpinned by a culture of care and opportunity.
Pastoral Care
Every pupil in our Senior School is encouraged to take on responsibility beyond the classroom. Whether helping lead their class to assembly, supporting peers during break times or acting as a tour guide for prospective families, these experiences help shape confident, articulate young people. Our strong pastoral structure, with small tutor groups and dedicated staff, ensures each pupil is supported as they grow in capability and independence.
Clubs and Activities
Discover Yateley Manor’s wide range of co-curricular clubs and activities. From sport and art to music, design, and outdoor adventures — there’s something for everyone.
Visit Yateley Manor
Whether you’re just starting your school search or looking for the right fit for your child, we’d love to welcome you.

Music at Yateley Manor
From the earliest years, pupils are encouraged to sing, perform and explore their creativity through a wide range of musical experiences. Weekly lessons build strong foundations in rhythm, pitch and listening. As pupils move through the school, they can learn an instrument, join choirs, or perform in one of our many ensembles.
Tuition and Ensembles
Our dedicated team of peripatetic music teachers offer one-to-one tuition in a variety of instruments, while choirs and instrumental groups rehearse weekly and perform throughout the year. Current ensembles include:
Pre-Prep Choir (Reception – Year 2)
Junior Manor Singers (Year 3-4)
Senior Manor Singers (Year 5-8)
Chamber Choir (Year 5-8, by invitation)
Beginner and Intermediate Strings (by invitation)
Wind Band
Percussion Group
Ukulele Group
Manor Rocks (rock band, by invitation)
MTech (music technology club)
Music Practice Club
Performance Opportunities
Concerts, recitals and school events give every pupil the chance to perform with confidence. Whether singing in a choir, playing in a concert, or performing as a soloist, pupils are encouraged to take pride in their progress and share their love of music.

Pre-Prep at Yateley Manor School
At Yateley Manor our Pre-Prep children flourish in a setting that combines stimulating learning with genuine care. Our aim is to enable each child to become a confident, well-educated individual with a lifelong enthusiasm for learning.
A Welcoming Learning Environment
Our Pre-Prep classrooms are bright, welcoming and full of opportunity. Each class is led by a dedicated class teacher, supported by a full-time teaching assistant, ensuring that children feel known, supported and engaged through a broad range of activities and subjects that make learning fun.
Building the Essentials
As children move into Year 1 and Year 2, we emphasise growing independence alongside academic progress. Daily phonics sessions, regular guided reading and a strong focus on writing and number work provide a firm foundation. Children are expected to be heard reading by an adult regularly, reinforcing confidence and fluency.
Connected Curriculum
Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed so learning is purposeful and interconnected. Topics link across subjects to give meaning and context, while discrete lessons — for example in mathematics and phonics — provide targeted teaching. Specialist subject teachers contribute to areas such as swimming and sport through our Games department.
Specialist Teaching & Broad Horizons
Even in Pre-Prep, children benefit from specialist teaching. Whether learning French, developing coordination in dance or improving fitness in PE, the experience is rich and varied. Every day brings an opportunity to build new skills and explore fresh interests.
Pastoral Care
At Yateley Manor Pre-Prep, pastoral care is woven into every part of school life. Our teachers take the time to know each child as an individual — their interests, their worries and what makes them shine. We create a safe, nurturing environment where children feel secure, valued and understood, building the confidence and resilience that will support them throughout their educational journey.
Looking Ahead to Prep School
At Yateley Manor, every child’s journey builds naturally from one stage to the next. As children move from Pre-Prep to Prep School, they take with them curiosity, confidence and a love of learning – ready to explore new subjects, develop independence and discover their individual strengths. In Prep, specialist teaching, wider opportunities and a nurturing environment ensure each child continues to thrive – academically, socially and personally — preparing them for the exciting years ahead

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep School at Yateley Manor | Years 3-6
pageCache.text:
Prep School at Yateley
As children join Yateley Manor in Years 3–6, our transition and pastoral arrangements are designed to welcome them quickly and securely into our school family. From the very start, new pupils feel recognised, supported and ready to flourish. Our aim is to develop happy, confident children who love learning. We celebrate each individual’s talents and achievements, while also nurturing areas for growth. By following this philosophy, our pupils become independent, self-assured young learners - prepared for the next phase of their journey.
Academic Spaces
Specialist classrooms and science labs designed to spark discovery and nurture a lifelong love of learning.
Creative Studios
From art and design to music and drama, our creative spaces encourage expression, confidence and collaboration.
Sport & Performance
Modern sports facilities and performance areas inspire children to challenge themselves, play with passion and celebrate every success.
Outdoor Learning & Wellbeing
Expansive grounds, adventure areas and calm corners provide space to think, explore and build resilience together.
Year 3 & 4
In Years 3 and 4, children are based in their own section of the school where classrooms are closely linked, creating a strong sense of community within their year group.
Pupils benefit from access to the full range of school facilities including -Art, Cookery, French and Music -helping them explore a wide variety of interests from early on.
Children are encouraged to participate in sport and begin inter-school matches, while their learning environment remains creative, nurturing and full of opportunity. We aim to provide school days that are vibrant and full of new experiences — from visiting ancient Celtic farms to imaginative role-play with a Roman legionnaire.
Year 5 & 6
As pupils move into Years 5 and 6, their learning accelerates in a setting shaped for growing independence and focus. In every subject, lessons are taught by specialists and pupils move around campus, gaining experience of different teaching styles, classrooms and learning contexts.
For those pupils moving on to senior schools at the end of Year 6, we offer a thorough support programme to help prepare them for entry examinations — ensuring they move forward with confidence and readiness.
Beyond the Classroom
Trips and Visits
Where learning leaps off the page. From museums and field studies to immersive history days, every trip brings subjects to life through adventure and experience.
Clubs & Activities
Where passions are discovered and talents grow. A rich programme of lunchtime and after-school clubs helps children try new things, build confidence, and follow their curiosity.
Outdoor Learning
Where challenges build character. Children explore nature, teamwork and leadership through forest activities, fieldwork and residential trips that inspire independence.
Performing Arts & Expression
Where every voice finds its stage. Music, drama and dance give children the freedom to perform, collaborate and shine with confidence.
Pastoral Care
Pastoral care is strong across the Prep School and becomes especially evident in Years 5 and 6. Tutor groups are small (typically around ten pupils), and the Form Tutor remains with the group for two years, supporting continuity of relationships, trust and understanding. The Form Tutor is the first point of contact for pastoral matters, though parents are welcome to engage with subject teachers directly for more specific discussions.
Looking Ahead to Senior School
As children move through Yateley Manor’s Prep School, they grow in independence, curiosity and confidence – ready to embrace the challenges and opportunities of Senior life. With specialist teaching, leadership roles and a rich co-curricular programme, pupils develop the skills, values and self-belief that prepare them for success in the years ahead. The transition to Senior School feels seamless – a continuation of the same supportive community where every child is known, encouraged and inspired to reach their potential

Each experience helps our pupils to grow in confidence and develop a deeper understanding of the world around them.

Working at Yateley Manor
At Yateley Manor, working here means joining more than a team — it means becoming part of a community built on respect, encouragement and shared purpose. We believe that strong relationships between staff and pupils are the cornerstone of our success, and we aim to support every member of our team in both professional growth and personal fulfilment.From the moment you arrive, you’ll find an environment where your ideas are heard, your development is prioritised and your role contributes meaningfully to pupils’ lives. Regular professional development, peer collaboration and a warm culture of support ensure that every colleague can thrive.
Whether you are a teacher, a member of our support staff, or part of our Early Years or holiday-camp teams, you will find purpose, challenge and reward in the work you do. At Yateley Manor we celebrate each other’s successes, encourage continuous improvement and look forward together to what pupils can achieve. Join us and find more than a job — find a place where your ambition, kindness and expertise are valued.
What our staff say
Our staff often tell us that Yateley Manor feels like much more than a workplace - it feels like a community where they are known, appreciated and able to contribute.
“I feel supported to try new ideas in my teaching and know that the whole team will back me.”
“Being part of Yateley Manor means being part of something special — the relationships with colleagues and pupils make such a difference.”
– Support Staff Member
Their experiences reflect a culture in which colleagues grow together, learn together and achieve together. Professional development is ongoing, with internal workshops, mentoring and opportunities for leadership roles. Every role at Yateley Manor is valued and every voice matters.

Life After Yateley Manor
The role of an excellent school is to prepare children for the next stage of their educational journey. Yateley Manor is proud of its reputation for supporting every child in admission to their first choice sixth form college. This is achieved through regular communication with parents and close relationships with a number of outstanding educational facilities.
Recent destinations for our senior pupils include:
Charterhouse School
Wellington College
Bradfield College
Lord Wandsworth College
Luckley House School
Frensham Heights
Eton College
Farnborough Hill
St George’s Ascot

Reading Blue Coat School
RGS (Royal Grammar School), Guildford
Yateley Manor Alumni
Yateley Manor has always been a school built on strong relationships, a shared sense of purpose and a genuine family spirit. This ethos has been at the heart of our community for over 75 years.
As part of our 75th anniversary celebrations, we launched the Yateley Manor Alumni Programme – a growing network of former pupils who remain part of the school’s story. Members receive updates throughout the year and are invited to special events that celebrate our past, present and future.
We know that many of our former pupils will enjoy seeing how the school has evolved while recognising the familiar warmth and values that make Yateley Manor so distinctive. Our Alumni aims to keep those connections alive, embracing the sense of family that has always defined us.
If you would like to join the Yateley Manor Alumni, please complete our short registration form and return it via email at [email protected] or via post to:
Jo Foster Yateley Manor School 51 Reading Road Yateley GU46 7UQ
Please remember to include your contact details so that we can keep you informed about future news and events.

Little Lodge Nursery at Yateley Manor School
At Little Lodge Nursery, every day is an adventure in learning and discovery. We provide a happy, nurturing environment where curiosity is encouraged, friendships flourish, and children feel confident to explore the world around them.
A message from our Nursery Manager
“From the moment I first stepped into Little Lodge, I knew it was a special place. The warmth of the children, the kindness of the staff and the sense of joy in every room made me feel instantly at home.
My passion has always been to give children the best possible start in life — helping them to grow in confidence, develop independence and love learning from the very beginning.”
Miss Kirsty Cordery Nursery Manager, Little Lodge Nursery
Trusted by Local Families
What Sets Little Lodge Apart
Our youngest learners benefit from Yateley Manor’s exceptional facilities, including access to the Woodland School, the school gym and the theatre for performances and assemblies.
What Sets Little Lodge Apart
Specialist teachers introduce children to subjects such as French, Dance and Physical Education, sparking curiosity and laying the foundations for future learning.
What Sets Little Lodge Apart
Our nursery has been thoughtfully designed to provide bright, well-equipped rooms and a large, imaginative outdoor play area -perfect for exploration, creativity and fun.
What Sets Little Lodge Apart
Little Lodge pupils are an important part of our wider school family. Older pupils often visit to read stories, help with activities and join in with events such as sports days, creating a strong sense of connection across the age groups.
What Sets Little Lodge Apart
When the time comes to move on, children are exceptionally well prepared for Reception. We offer transition mornings and parent information sessions to ensure the process feels calm, familiar and exciting. For families moving to other schools, our team provides support and guidance every step of the way.
Useful Information
Settling In
Starting nursery is a big step – for children and parents alike. To help every child feel comfortable, we offer three settling-in sessions during the week before their start date.
The first session includes a meeting with your child’s key person, with parents staying for 30 minutes before leaving briefly.
The following two sessions are completed independently by the child, helping them build confidence and familiarity. Further information about our settling-in process is available upon request.
Parent Communication
We value strong partnerships with parents. Each child has a personal online learning journal through Family, where parents can view daily updates on their child’s learning, care routines and achievements. Parents can also message their child’s key worker directly at any time. Additional nursery news is shared weekly through our parent newsletter, INAMOS.
Transition to Reception
Children moving into Reception enjoy a smooth, supported transition. During the summer term, they take part in three settling-in sessions with the Reception team, meeting teachers and current pupils while exploring their new classroom environment.
This thoughtful approach ensures children begin the next stage of their journey happy, confident and ready to shine.
Fees & Admissions
To find out our current fee structure, register entrance or arrange a nursery visit, please contact the Nursery Office using the enquiry form below.

Our Values
The values of our school are like a heartbeat for everybody. Values guide our actions, so they are in alignment with our beliefs. They also connect us to the core of who we are. At Yateley Manor we have six core values which run through our community. They help guide the way we are with one another; they channel our behaviour and bring the community together to provide children with opportunities which will lead to successful adult lives.
Happiness
Happiness means finding joy and satisfaction in everyday life. It looks different for everyone, but it always involves positivity, gratitude, and a sense of fulfilment. Even in challenging times, happy people hold onto optimism – trusting that they can overcome difficulties and find joy again.
Reflectiveness
Being reflective allows us to learn deeply and meaningfully. Reflection helps us make sense of our experiences, connecting what we learn in the classroom with the world around us. It builds insight, understanding and a lifelong curiosity for learning.
Community
Community is at the heart of who we are. It gives us a sense of belonging, shared purpose and pride. At Yateley Manor, everyone matters – each individual contributes to the spirit, character and strength of our community.
Resilience
Resilience is the strength to keep going when things don’t go to plan. It helps us face challenges, learn from setbacks and find enjoyment in life. Resilient people don’t see failure as defeat, but as an opportunity to grow and improve.
Teamwork
Teamwork is about working together towards a shared goal. It brings out the best in everyone by combining different strengths, ideas and perspectives. Learning to collaborate effectively is a vital skill that children carry with them throughout life.
Relationships
Strong relationships are the foundation of a thriving school. They inspire motivation, nurture confidence and create a sense of trust and belonging. At Yateley Manor, our relationships – between children and adults alike – are built on care, challenge, support and mutual respect.

pageCache.pageTitle: Academics at Yateley Manor School. Curiosity, Confidence and Character
pageCache.text:
Academics at Yateley Manor
We believe every child should feel inspired to think independently, ask questions and enjoy the process of discovery. Our journey begins in Nursery and continues through to Senior School, with each stage designed to stretch, support and celebrate every pupil.
Our curriculum goes beyond the National Curriculum. As an independent school we are free to design a rich programme of learning that connects subjects, brings real-world relevance and invites deeper thinking. For example, children may code a computer game and create its soundtrack or explore 3D art inspired by everyday materials.
Small class sizes and specialist teachers ensure that every pupil receives the attention and challenge they need. The result is more than excellent examination outcomes: it is a child who leaves us ready for whatever comes next, with confidence, intellectual curiosity and strong character.
Attitude to Learning
At Yateley Manor we believe that how a child learns is as important as what they learn. We measure and nurture the ‘attitude to learning’ through key indicators such as engagement, preparation, punctuality and perseverance.
Our four-point grading system for Attitude to Learning (A–D) is a clear framework for improvement. Grades are recorded every four weeks so that families stay informed about both academic progress and the learning behaviours that underpin success.
The focus on learning behaviours means pupils develop beyond the classroom: they learn to collaborate effectively, ask for support when needed, stay focused during a task and reflect on their own progress. This builds resilient, self-aware learners who carry their growth mindset into Senior School and beyond.
Preparing for life beyond the classroom
Qualifications remain important, but we know they are not everything. At Yateley Manor we educate the whole child -academic, practical, creative and personal. We support pupils to become not just high achievers but people of integrity, self-confidence and purpose.
From the earliest years to the final year, children are encouraged to take ownership of their learning. They learn to reflect, adapt and improve. At Senior level, they often lead in school life, present to different audiences and take responsibility for their environment.
Why it Matters
By the time our pupils leave Yateley Manor, they are well-prepared for the next stage of their education -but more than that, they are ready to learn for life. They have honed the habits of mind and the confidence to thrive in unfamiliar environments, to take part in debate, to initiate ideas and to be resilient in the face of challenge.
